failure_masking_mechanism.finding: MockServer Drop synchronously verifies every mounted expectation. On ordinary return with unmatched requests it panics; if the thread is already panicking it only logs the verification error. Therefore a fallible Result return can be obscured by the reported mock verification, without establishing what that original error was.

tests.analysis: The raw log shows six MCP requests including both skill resource reads, one skill analytics request, three suggested-plugin requests and two model requests. Thus the first two model responses were consumed. Before the second submit_turn, the fixture validates fallible resource-access/read JSON and Code Mode output shape/JSON. The bridge supplies the actual Code Mode host prerequisite, but the original output text and original returned Result error are absent. A Code Mode fallback/error is a compatible hypothesis, not a proved cause; the second-submit boundary also remains unlocalized.
